text:
maria: FYI customer reported repeated 504s and 5xx from hosted API between 10:12-10:22 UTC, they hit timeouts when traffic spiked. Escalating.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-3790001. Pager rung to oncall. :rotating_light:
support-ops: Customer says they see 30-60s latencies then 504 gateway. They included curl with x-request-id header.
maria: Attached logs show proxy returning 502/504 after backend timed out waiting for model pod.
eli: Can you paste the scaledobject + hpa annotations for that tenant? Need to check KEDA triggers and cooldown.
maria: Here are the relevant k8s objects (sanitized):
```
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: tenant-abc-scaledobject
  annotations:
    autoscaling.alpha.kubernetes.io/behavior: '{"scaleDown": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds": 300}}'
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: tenant-abc-deployment
  triggers:
  - type: external
    metadata:
      metricName: rps
      targetValue: "100"
      query: tenant_abc_rps
```

jess: Noted. HPA is using CPU target while KEDA external metric expects "requests-per-second" in telemetry. Metric naming mismatch looks likely. If KEDA never sees the metric above threshold, it won't scale fast.
devin: Also seeing readinessProbe in pod spec uses initialDelaySeconds: 10 and a heavy init that pulls ~1.2s per model shard. Coldstarts can add ~15s. Combined with KEDA poll interval (60s) and KEDA scale-up cooldown 30s, we can easily get >30s of unready pods causing gateway timeouts.
maria: Customer traffic pattern was a sharp burst (sudden 300% over baseline) from their integration test.
eli: Repro plan: 1) simulate RPS spike using wrk with header tenant id 2) watch KEDA metrics and scaledobject 3) observe pods init + readiness timeline 4) capture proxy 502/504.
devin: Commands to repro (run from bastion):
```bash
wrk -t2 -c200 -d60s -H "x-tenant: tenant_abc" http://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate
kubectl get scaledobject tenant-abc-scaledobject -o yaml
kubectl describe hpa tenant-abc-deployment
kubectl logs -n infer deployment/tenant-abc --since=10m --tail=200
```

jess: Temporary mitigation: increase KEDA poll frequency to 15s, set cooldownSeconds to 5 for that tenant, and add prewarm annotation: "redwood.io/prewarm: \"true\"" on the scaledobject to keep a warm replica pool. Also bump minReplicas to 2.
maria: Did that for the customer's Dedicated pool (applied via infra patch). Monitoring now.
support-ops: Customer confirmed fewer 504s after changes but still saw two spikes at 10:46 and 10:49 with transient 502s.
eli: Next root cause step: telemetry shows external metric export failed between 10:11-10:14 (auth token rotation returned 403 to metrics exporter). If metrics exporter couldn't push the RPS metric, KEDA would see zeros and not scale.
devin: Yep, auth rotation + metrics exporter outage + metric name mismatch = hysteresis. For long term: 1) fail-open for metrics exporter (so KEDA uses HPA fallback), 2) align metric names and add unit tests for scaledobject templates, 3) reduce readiness probe initialDelay or split heavy model init into background lazy load.
jess: I'll open a PR to standardize annotation templates and add a CI check to validate scaledobject metric names against exporter mapping.
maria: Customer asked for timeline and repro — compiling now. Will include kubectl dumps and wrk commands.
ops-bot: Update: INC-3790001 -> mitigated (partial) at 3790001600, monitoring.
support-ops: Customer requested credit for the 10-minute outage window. Sending to billing ops.
eli: Postmortem items: runbook update for coldstart bursts, add prewarm option to tenant onboarding, and an alert when external metric exporter returns >=5 4xx/5xx in 5m.
maria: Thanks team — keeping this thread open until postmortem drafted.
